text:
maya: Heads-up — signal explorer shows a flatline for bert-qa-v2 run (quantize-8bit) on the run-summary heatmap starting at step ~1200. Looks like token_latency and latency_bucket counts drop to 0 for many shards.
alex: I saw that too. Diff panel also missing the "sample_breakdown" rows for that run id.
jordan: CI runner logs had a warning earlier: `ingest: dropped 28 rows (null metric)` — could be related. Pasting tail:```
2026-03-18T15:22:12Z runner INFO ingest start
2026-03-18T15:22:19Z runner WARN metric_parse: null for token_latency at sample_id=...
2026-03-18T15:22:21Z runner INFO ingest complete, accepted=872, dropped=28
```
li: Is this only for quantize-8bit? or also for fp16 baseline?
maya: Baseline fp16 shows normal buckets. Only quantized variant (bert-qa-v2:q8) shows the gap.
kevin: Could be a change in the runner aggregator that skips empty kv-cache metrics. I remember a recent PR that gated token_latency emission when kv_cache was missing.
sophia: Analytics bot — any telemetry anomalies?
analytics-bot: ingest_pipeline.errors.count increased by +28 for job:runner/quantize-8bit/2026-03-18. Top tag: metric=null_value.
alex: Repro suggestion — re-run the ingest for that CI artifact with seed=42 and metrics=token_latency,token_count to see if we still drop rows. Command:```
./eval-runner --artifact=gs://redwood-evals/bert-qa-v2/q8/2026-03-18 --split=dev --seed=42 --metrics=token_latency,token_count --emit-kv=true
```
jordan: Also check dashboard bucketizer: the heatmap bucket keys are generated by `bucketize(latency, [0,5,10,20,50,100])` — if latency is null the bucket becomes "unbucketed" and we filter those out in the run-summary aggregator. Maybe the aggregator should include an "unbucketed" lane instead of dropping.
li: Quick fix idea: change aggregator filter from `where bucket is not null` to `where run_status='completed'` and surface unbucketed counts in a collapsed row in the UI.
kevin: I can prototype that in the aggregator service — minimal change. But we should confirm root cause first: why is token_latency null for q8 only?
sophia: Could be quantization pipeline dropping per-token timings because of fused kernels. We had an opt that disabled per-token instrumentation for certain kernel paths (PR #4021).
alex: If that's the case, we should add a metric-emission shim in the runner to synthesize token_latency from `wall_ms / token_count` when per-token timings disabled — mark as approximate.
jordan: Agree. For the immediate triage: 1) rehydrate the missing rows so dashboards render, 2) patch aggregator to keep unbucketed counts, 3) longer-term add shim + unit tests.
maya: I'm re-running the ingest now with alex's command. Will post results.
maya: Re-run finished — `accepted=900, dropped=0`. Heatmap shows lanes repopulated. Looks like the dropped rows were specific to that artifact ingestion attempt.
analytics-bot: ingest_pipeline.reingest.success for job:runner/quantize-8bit/2026-03-18 (triggered by maya)
li: Since this happened once, we should add a CI check: after ingest, assert `dropped_rows == 0` and fail the eval job otherwise. That would catch future flaps.
kevin: +1. I'll add a post-ingest assertion hook in the runner (small change).
sophia: Also add an alert in Console: when heatmap bucket coverage < 90% for a model-run, create a warning in the run-summary tile.
alex: For the dashboard change, UX note — don't show an error toast for users viewing older runs; show a small badge "partial metrics" with tooltip.
maya: Filed follow-ups: ENG-ML-569 (aggregator: show unbucketed), ENG-ML-570 (runner: post-ingest assertion), ENG-ML-571 (shim for token_latency synth), ENG-ML-572 (console: partial metrics badge).
jordan: Can we add a tiny smoke test to the eval-harness CI that runs a 1-shot quantize-8bit pipeline and verifies metric emission? That would have caught this earlier.
alex: Agree, adding to CI. I'll scope it as a lightweight job with mocked kernels.
kevin: I'll put up a draft PR for the aggregator fix and the post-ingest hook today.
maya: Thanks team. If anyone sees other runs with similar gaps, ping here and tag me. :thumbsup:
